data.name: Vineeth
data.gender_notes: Vineeth is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Vineeth is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Vijnana' which means 'knowledge' or 'wisdom'. It is also associated with the Tamil word 'Ven' which means 'healer'. This name symbolizes the victory of knowledge over ignorance and the strength of a healer who helps others in their time of need. The name Vineeth carries the meaning “Healer, Victor” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil, Malayalam. Parents who choose Vineeth usually hope their child will grow to embody healer, victor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Vineeth is a name that embodies the spiritual qualities of wisdom, knowledge, and healing. It is a name that inspires one to seek knowledge and understanding, and to use this knowledge to help others in their time of need.
data.etymology: Vineeth belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Healer, Victor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vineeth total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

historical_references.reference: Vineet was a prominent Jaina scholar and philosopher from Karnataka, India. He contributed significantly to Jaina literature in the 13th century AD, during the Hoysala Empire. He wrote various commentaries and texts, including the 'Tattvartha Sutra Bhashya'.
historical_references.context: Hoysala Empire, Jaina Scholar and Philosopher

historical_references.reference: Vineeth (Vidyaranya) was a great Hindu sage and reformer, who played a crucial role in the revival of Hinduism in the 14th century AD, during the Vijayanagara Empire. He is known for his works such as 'Mahabharata' commentary and 'Amuktamalyada'.
historical_references.context: Vijayanagara Empire, Hindu Sage and Reformer
